name: Hatipha
overview: Hatipha was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role is noted in the context of the post-exilic community, emphasizing his service in the house of God. Beyond his tribal affiliation and temple service, no additional personal details are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Hatipha means "taken captive," reflecting a Hebrew proper name without indication of divine origin. This meaning may suggest a historical or familial background related to captivity, but the Scripture only records the name itself.
familyAndRelationships: Hatipha is identified as a descendant of Levi, indicating his Levitical heritage. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond this tribal connection and his role as a temple servant.
scriptureSignificance: Hatipha's significance lies in his role as a temple servant from the tribe of Levi during the restoration period, highlighting the reestablishment of temple worship among the returning exiles. His mention underscores the continuity of Levitical service in God's house and the faithfulness of those who returned to fulfill their duties in the post-exilic community.
